title: Open extension and scalar restriction preserve the normalized scalar counit
statement:
Let $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion of schemes and $A\to B$ a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Use ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ of constant-ring module sheaves, for $W=X,Z$ and $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Put $T_W=-\otimes^L_{A_W}B_W$ and let $r_W$ be exact scalar restriction, with the representative-normalized adjunction $T_W\dashv r_W$ and counit $\epsilon_W$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Write $J_R=j_{!,R}$ for the sheafified extension-by-zero construction [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and its exact derived adjunction $J_R\dashv j_R^{-1}$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Let $a_L:J_Ar_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}r_ZJ_BL$ be the canonical sectionwise restriction-of-scalars comparison of that node. Let $E_M:T_ZJ_AM\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT_XM$ be the canonical open tensor comparison, normalized by its balanced tensor map on the open, as in [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison].
The unit $M\to j_R^{-1}J_RM$ is the identity under the sectionwise identification on objects over $X$, for every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$; in particular restriction to $X$ determines a derived arrow with source $J_RM$ through this adjunction. Under these unit identifications and the canonical restriction/tensor and restriction/scalar identifications, $j_B^{-1}E_M$ and $j_A^{-1}a_L$ are identity comparisons. For every ambient $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ one has the scalar counit equation
$$\epsilon_Z(J_BL)\circ T_Z(a_L)=J_B(\epsilon_X(L))\circ E_{r_XL}.$$
The isomorphisms $a,E$ and this equation are natural in their derived arguments. For the identity ring homomorphism they are the identity comparisons under the canonical scalar unitors. These assertions require no flatness of $B/A$, boundedness, constructibility or Tor condition on $L$ or $r_XL$.

proof.text: The intrinsic sheaf extension is fully faithful by transport of the proved finite-coefficient extension-by-zero full/faithful instances. Thus its open unit is invertible. Compute the exact localized unit on cochain representatives with Adjunction.localization_unit_app and the identity and composition factor equations. This identifies it with sfIntrinsicDerivedOpenUnit. Prove that exact localization preserves the unit equation for leftAdjointUniq, using normalizedAdjunction_uniqueness and the localized Hom formula. Apply this to reductionOpenModel to identify the transported constant-coordinate unit with that same intrinsic unit. Its invertibility follows. Equality of restrictions of arrows with open-extended source gives equality of adjuncts, hence equality of arrows by injectivity of the open Hom equivalence.

The scalar restriction unit equation is exactly lem-sp-open-scalar-restriction-unit in the coordinates of openScalarCounitAdjunction. It is strictly the scalar restriction half of openScalarCounitRestriction; it contains no tensor comparison or scalar counit equation.

For the tensor unit equation, use the two open and two scalar adjunctions. Expand the unit equation of the left-adjoint uniqueness comparison defining openScalarIso, then use naturality of its right-adjoint comparison and the scalar mate unit equation. Injectivity of the scalar Hom equivalence proves scalarOpenTranspose. Transport both open left adjoints by reductionOpenModel: cancel the inverse/hom of the B-coordinate change, and apply naturality of inverse lambda at the inverse A-coordinate change. This proves the tensor restriction equation, independently of the tensor-normalization theorem.

For the scalar counit square, precompose both arrows by the inverse open tensor comparison, putting their common source into open-extended form. Apply the B-open Hom equivalence. Rewrite its unit using the tensor equation of Step 3, move inverse lambda by naturality, and use mateEquiv_counit_symm. This Mathlib formula applies directly because inverse tensorPullbackIso is definitionally the inverse scalar mate of rightSquare.inv. The scalar restriction equation of Step 2 and naturality of the scalar counit make the two adjuncts equal. Injectivity, cancellation and natural-transformation extensionality give the asserted square.

For the identity coefficient map, apply the existing derived identity law for sfOpenRestrictionDerived. The left-adjoint uniqueness counit formula identifies each scalar counit with the composite of the scalar and restriction unitors. Substitute these into the square of Step 4; naturality of the ambient scalar unitor and cancellation of the restriction unitor prove the tensor identity on restricted objects. Naturality at the restriction unitor extends it to every object. These calculations use no boundedness or flatness and include empty opens, whole opens and zero objects.

Step 5: the lambda factors match on both sides, and precomposing with E^{-1} makes the source an open extension, so injectivity applies. Step 6: identity case via lem-fix 'including identities' and representative formula (2). Types verified throughout. Coefficient categories (constant finite R, ordinary unbounded pro-etale) are the same as in def-sp and lem-fix. Edge cases: empty X, X=Z, nonflat Z/4->Z/2, A=B. lean.statement: theorem openScalarCounitSquare {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B] (φ : A →+* B) {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : X ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion j] : Functor.whiskerRight (sfOpenRestrictionDerived j φ).hom (scalarExtensionFunctor φ Z) ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero j B).mapDerivedCategory (proEtaleRingDerivedExtensionAdjunction (proEtaleConstantRingMap (T := Z) φ)).counit = Functor.whiskerLeft (scalarRestriction φ X) (reductionOpenScalarIso φ j).hom ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (proEtaleRingDerivedExtensionAdjunction (proEtaleConstantRingMap (T := X) φ)).counit (sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero j B).mapDerivedCategory
